title: The class number one theorem without Heegner, kernel-checked: d <= 652 from the 7/8 quasi-Riemann hypothesis in Lean 4
description:
Lean 4 formalization, certificate generators, numerical checks and a paper proving the class number one theorem for imaginary quadratic fields without Heegner's method: for squarefree m ≥ 1, Q(√−m) has class number one if and only if m ∈ {1, 2, 3, 7, 11, 19, 43, 67, 163}. Written for T. Tao's tenth-discriminant AI-math challenge of 20 October 2026.

Route. Under class number one, the Dedekind zeta function is half an Epstein zeta function and equals ζ(s)L(s,χ). The Chowla–Selberg formula, with an explicit remainder proved in Lean, continues it to s = 7/8. OpenAI's zero-free region Re s > 7/8 for Dirichlet L-functions (openai/math, family 003, commit adc7f124) gives L(7/8,χ) ≥ 0 while ζ(7/8) < 0, forcing d ≤ 652, proved in Lean about Mathlib's riemannZeta and Gamma. Kernel-checked split-prime witnesses dispose of the 190 remaining fields, and the Minkowski bound proves the converse for the nine. The route was worked out in the comments of Tao's post; the credits are in the README.

Verification. The statement uses only Mathlib definitions. The proof depends only on propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. Comparator (leanprover/comparator v4.34.0) accepts it under two independent kernels, nanoda and Lean's, and rejects tampered statements. OpenAI's Lean proof of the 7/8 theorem is inside the checked dependency closure, not an assumption. The runs were local and not sandboxed.

Status. Not refereed. OpenAI's manuscript is unrefereed, although its Lean proof is kernel-checked. The work was produced with extensive AI assistance (Claude, Anthropic), with independent AI review; see the README.
